issues.description: Constructor signature for class SealSaloon differs between the problem statement and the solution. The problem statement (UML and explanatory text) specifies a constructor SealSaloon(String) that accepts the saloon name as a String (used for identification). The solution implementation defines a no-argument constructor public SealSaloon() instead. This inconsistency leaves students unsure whether they must implement a constructor that takes a String parameter and may lead to mismatches with tests or grading code that expect the named constructor.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor signatures consistent. Either (A) update the solution (and template) to provide a constructor public SealSaloon(String name) that initializes the instance fields (e.g., orders) and stores/uses the provided name, or (B) revise the problem statement and UML to allow a no-argument constructor. Preferred student-facing fix: require and implement public SealSaloon(String name) in SealSaloon, initialize orders to an empty Meal[] in that constructor, and keep the shared static stock as specified.
